main_text.l: maleficii, nec diffitetem obscoenis sestu-duisse doctrinis, nocturnos etiam turpiu foeminarum egisse conventus, nuduMq; orare solitum, nocentem pronunciavit, redegitq; in custodiam donec ad principe referret. Gestis ad palatium delatis, censuit imperator, Priscillianum iocisq; ejus capitis damnari oportere. Ceterum Ithacius videns, quam invidiosum sibi apud episcopos foret, si accusato, etiam postremis rerum capitalium judiciis astitisset (etenim iterari judicium necesse erat) subtrahit se cognitioni frustra calido jam sece lere perfecto[?]. At tum per Maximum accusator apponitur Patricius quidam, fisci patronus. Ita eo infistente, Priscillianus capitis damnatus est, unaq; cum eo Felicisimus & Armenius, qui nuper a catholicis, clerici Priscillianum secuti, desciverant. Latronianus quoq; & Euchro-cia gladio perempti. Instantius, quem superius ab episcopis damnatum diximus, in Sylinam infulam, quæ ultra Britanniam sita est, deportatus. Itum deinde in reliquos sequentibus judiciis, damnatiquè Asurinus & Aurelius diaconus gladio. Tyberianus, ademptis bonis, in Sy-

page.notes: Page number at head read as 176; the digits are partly worn, so [?]. Running head repeated as printed. "lere" in "lere perfecto" is doubtful; it may be "iure" or another word, so [?]. The catchword "linam" completes "Sylinam" begun at the line end ("Sy-"). Left-margin notes are only partly legible: "hæretici", "a Maximo capitis damnati", and the notes at the Latronianus and Tyberianus lines are read with doubt; the reference notes at the foot are transcribed roughly and not reliably. "Asurinus" in the text is read as Afrinus/Afarinus, so it may be misread; the scan is unclear there. Printed spellings such as "obscoenis", "conventus", and "Sylinam" are left as printed. Some passages of the text are heavily worn and uncertain.
